```{r}
#| label: setup

options(scipen = 1, knitr.kable.NA = "")

# Load necessary packages
library(tidyverse)
```

This page showcases the geospatial analysis, which uses a map of the entire US (including Alaska and Hawaii). This visualization was obtained using the "usmap" package because the regular "maps" package did not provide Alaska and Hawaii in its visualization. The coordinates of each institution was provided by @collegecoordinates and the overall data (financial aid and salaries of men and women) was obtained by the U.S. Department of Education (@rawdata). The implications of these visualizations can help us understand regional disparities across the United States, which builds off of the initial box plot visualization that gives us a more general idea of the disparities between men and women.

```{r}
load("data/danielVisualization.Rdata")
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Tab 1


```{r}
#| fig-cap: "From the visualization, we can see that institutions located in the SouthEast tend to have a higher disparity favored towards men. In other words, male students tend to recieve more financial aid than women at institutions in the SouthEast. On the contrary, institutions located in the West tend to have little-to-no disparities as indicated by the lighter colors compared to the darker ones in the East. From this information, it can be argued that most institutions do not have direct biases against a particular gender when it comes to distributing financial aid. We will see, in the next visualization, that this is not the case for head coach salaries."
# From geospatial lab (but using usmaps instead)
plot_usmap(fill = "lightgrey", color = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = aid_transformed,
          aes(color = male_female_aid_ratio),
              size = 3) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1,
                     labels = scales::label_number()) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(color = "",
       title = "Ratio of Male vs. Female Aid for D1 Institutions"
  )
```



### Tab 2


```{r}
#| fig-cap: "From the second visualization, we can see that, unlike financial aid, most institutions tend to pay male head coaches more than female head coaches which is indicated by the dark red colors all over the map with a few exceptions in the East. Inversely, we can also deduce that none of the institutions on the map pay a higher salary towards women indiciated by the absence of blue dots on the map. From this visualization and the apparent difference between the salaries of head coaches, we can firmly state that, even in the year 2026 where we try to advocate for gender equality, there are still huge pay gaps in America. This, I argue, should be an issue addressed or at least looked over to remove as many imbalances in the NCAA as possible."
# From geospatial lab (but using usmaps instead)
plot_usmap(fill = "lightgrey", color = "white") +
  geom_sf(data = HDCOACH_transformed,
          aes(color = male_female_salary_ratio),
              size = 3) +
  scale_color_distiller(palette = "Spectral",
                        limits = c(0, 5), # Forces scale to start at 1
                        oob = scales::squish, # Groups points that are out of bounds to the nearest scaled number (i.e. 15x is not on the scale so it groups it to 5x).
                     labels = scales::label_number()) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(color = "",
       title = "Ratio of Male vs. Female Head Coach Salaries for D1 Institutions"
  )
```


:::
